issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs that the Animal name getter and setter should use protected visibility (to allow subclass access but prevent external access), but the solution implementation declares getName() and setName(...) as public. This is a structural visibility mismatch between the specification and the provided solution and can confuse students about the intended access level for these methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the visibility of getName() and setName(...) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java from public to protected to match the problem statement. Alternatively, if public visibility is intended, update the problem statement/UML to state public visibility for these methods.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates a protected constructor for Animal (marked with '#'), but the solution implements the Animal(String) constructor as public. This visibility difference conflicts with the UML/specification and may mislead students about the intended constructor accessibility for an abstract base class.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Animal(String) constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java from public to protected to align with the UML/specification. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to indicate a public constructor if that is the intended design.
